results.evidence: `get_stored_untagged_followup_mode` returns None for no row or empty column. The webhook gate only drops on `!= UntaggedFollowupMode.NEVER`, so unset passes. In the activity, `mode` None is neither AUTO nor NEVER, so it reaches `_post_untagged_followup_prompt(...)` and returns True.

The activity keeps `if mode == AUTO: return False` (forward, no prompt) and `if mode == NEVER: ... return True` (ignore, no prompt, whatever the replier). ASK still falls through to the prompt. The webhook gate still drops NEVER.

The prompt always has 'Yes, take a look' and 'No thanks'. With `offer_default` it adds 'Yes, always' and 'No, never', which call `_save_untagged_followup_default` with AUTO or NEVER. `offer_default=mode is None and slack_user_id == mapping.mentioning_slack_user_id`, so only the thread creator sees the save buttons. That matches the setting being the creator's.

`_untagged_followups_section_blocks(mode)` sets `initial_option` from `mode.value`, and `resolve_untagged_followup_mode` now returns ASK when unset. The caller that decides whether to render the section is not shown, so I can't confirm the section is rendered for users with no stored setting.

An unrecognised value now falls to `return None` in `get_stored_untagged_followup_mode`. The activity treats None as unset and prompts, and `resolve_untagged_followup_mode` returns ASK. The old behaviour, where it resolved to NEVER, is gone.

The prompt text is 'I'm working in this thread. Want me to pick up your message? Only you can see this — nothing happens unless you say so.' It has no mention of where to change the setting and no link. `app_home_url` is imported in api.py but not used in the prompt.

The patch does not touch quota handling. Whether an unconfirmed untagged reply is already stopped silently over quota, while mentions and confirmed replies get the denial message, depends on code that isn't shown.

result:
A Slack user who has never set a thread follow-up preference now gets the "pick up your message?" prompt when they reply without tagging PostHog. I haven't run any tests, and `ruff` isn't installed here, so nothing was linted or formatted. I only checked that the changed Python files compile. The existing tests may also still assume the old behaviour (unset means never), so run them before merging.

- **Unset now means ask.** Someone with no preference used to be treated as "never", so the reply was dropped before the prompt logic ran. The webhook and the workflow now drop a reply only when the thread creator's stored choice is explicitly "never". Unset goes through the same classifier and prompt as "ask".
- **Explicit choices are unchanged.** People who already picked "auto", "ask" or "never" behave exactly as before.
- **New prompt buttons.** When the setting is unset and the replier is the thread creator, the prompt adds "Yes, always" and "No, never". These save "auto" or "never" as the default, and "Yes, always" also sends the message. The buttons are only offered to the creator because the creator's setting is the one that governs the thread.
- **Home page.** The existing "Thread follow-ups" picker already showed and saved this setting. It now shows "Ask them first" for an unset user instead of "Leave them alone", so what it displays matches what actually happens.

I updated `products/slack_app/backend/tests/services/test_slack_settings.py` for the new meaning of unset. I didn't add tests for the new buttons or the save-default handlers.

The main changes are in `products/slack_app/backend/api.py` (prompt, button handlers, webhook gate), `posthog/temporal/ai/slack_app/activities/messaging.py` and `services/slack_settings.py`, which gains `get_stored_untagged_followup_mode` to tell "unset" apart from "never".
